prompts.q: Which command shows free and used disk space per mounted filesystem?
prompts.note: -h prints sizes in human-readable units (GB/MB) instead of raw 1K blocks. “Disk is full — which mount?” → df. “What is eating this mount?” → du.

prompts.q: df -h shows plenty of free space, yet writes fail with "No space left on device". Which df flag reveals the likely cause?
prompts.note: Inode usage — a filesystem can run out of inodes with bytes to spare.

prompts.q: Which journalctl flag streams new log entries live, like `tail -f`?
Only SSH entries from the last hour: journalctl -u ssh {{--since}} "1 hour ago"
prompts.note: Takes human-friendly time expressions: "1 hour ago", "yesterday", "2026-01-01".

prompts.q: Using ps, snapshot every running process and filter to lines mentioning nginx — what is the classic pipeline?
prompts.note: pgrep -a nginx is the tidier purpose-built alternative.

prompts.q: In `ps aux`, which letter includes daemons — processes with no controlling terminal?
prompts.note: a = all users' processes, u = user-oriented columns (CPU/mem).

prompts.q: Which modern command shows a machine's IP addresses and network interfaces?
prompts.note: Short form: ip a. Successor to the older ifconfig.

prompts.q: View the routing table, including the default gateway — what do you run?
prompts.note: Short form: ip r. The "default via …" line is the gateway.

prompts.q: What permissions does `chmod 644 file.txt` set?
prompts.note: Owner read+write, group and others read-only. Read=4, write=2, execute=1; each octal digit is one of owner/group/others.

prompts.q: Add execute permission to a script without changing any other bits — what do you run?
Which command refreshes the local package index, and should usually run before `apt install`?
prompts.note: Otherwise install resolves against a stale index.

prompts.q: Which apt subcommand actually installs the newer versions of all installed packages?
prompts.note: update only refreshes the index; upgrade does the installing.

prompts.q: Search a whole directory tree for "TODO", showing file names and line numbers — what do you run?
prompts.note: -r recurses, -n adds line numbers, -i would ignore case.

prompts.q: Which grep flag inverts the match — printing lines that do NOT contain the pattern?
prompts.note: e.g. `grep -v "^#"` strips comment lines from a config file.

prompts.q: Which command shows how much RAM and swap are currently in use?
In free's output, which column shows memory the kernel can actually give to new processes (reclaimable cache included)?
prompts.note: The "free" column alone looks alarmingly low on healthy systems — page cache counts as used.

prompts.q: Inside less, how do you search forward for the text "failed"?
prompts.note: `?failed` searches backward; n / N repeat the search forward / backward.

prompts.q: Inside less, which key jumps to the end of the file (the newest log lines)?
prompts.note: Lowercase g jumps back to the top. `less +G file` opens already at the end.

prompts.q: Which tail flag keeps the file open and prints new lines as they are appended, in real time?
prompts.note: Plain tail prints the last 10 lines and exits. -F additionally survives log rotation.

prompts.q: Show the last 100 lines, then keep streaming new ones: tail {{-n 100 -f}} file.log
Which sudo flag runs the command as a specific non-root user?
prompts.note: e.g. sudo -u postgres psql

prompts.q: What is the only safe way to edit /etc/sudoers (the file defining who may use sudo)?
prompts.note: It syntax-checks before saving — a broken sudoers can lock everyone out of root.

prompts.q: Delete logs untouched for over 30 days: find /var/log -name "*.log" {{-mtime +30}} -delete
prompts.note: +30 = modified more than 30 days ago. Run without -delete first to preview.

prompts.q: Find every file larger than 100 MB under / — what do you run?
What does kiitos mean?
What does anteeksi mean?
Two casual ways to say 'hi' in Finnish?
How many ways can a Finnish letter be pronounced?
prompts.note: Fully phonemic: every letter is always pronounced, always the same way — never silent, never context-dependent.

prompts.q: What is the technical term for a spelling system where one letter always equals one sound?
prompts.note: Finnish spelling is fully phonemic — if you can spell it, you can say it: kioski.

prompts.q: What does talo mean?
Finnish for 'house'?
talo + “in the house” = talo{{ssa}}
prompts.note: Back-vowel word takes -ssa; no gradation — talo is the clean model noun for the case grid.

prompts.q: Which three letters are Finnish's front vowels?
prompts.note: They are independent letters, not accented a/o/u.

prompts.q: Which three letters are the back vowels?
prompts.note: e and i are neutral — they pair with either set.

prompts.q: Which rule says a native word's vowels must be all back or all front, never mixed?
prompts.note: e/i are neutral and go with either set: talossa (back) vs metsässä (front).

prompts.q: metsä + “in the forest” = metsä{{ssä}}
prompts.note: Front-vowel word (ä) takes the front form -ssä; back-vowel talo takes -ssa: talossa.

prompts.q: What does kauppa mean?
Finnish for 'shop'?
Apply the genitive: kauppa + -n → ?
prompts.note: pp→p — the textbook KPT example.

prompts.q: In consonant gradation, what are the two grades a stem alternates between?
prompts.note: Called KPT because it hits the stops k, p, t; the basic form is strong, most endings trigger the weak grade.

prompts.q: Which grade appears when an ending closes the syllable (like genitive -n)?
prompts.note: kauppa → kaupan

prompts.q: Which two endings keep the strong grade instead of weakening it?
prompts.note: Partitive -a/-ä and the illative don't close the preceding syllable the same way.

prompts.q: pp weakens to what in the weak grade?
prompts.note: kauppa → kaupan (shop)

prompts.q: kauppa + -n (genitive) = kau{{pa}}n
prompts.note: pp → p — the canonical KPT example (shop).

prompts.q: Which syllable of a Finnish word carries the stress?
prompts.note: Every word, no exceptions — even long loanwords.

prompts.q: Mark the stress: Kalevala → ?
prompts.note: First syllable, always.

prompts.q: The s-cases (-ssa/-sta/-Vn) translate which three English prepositions?
prompts.note: Interior cases: talossa · talosta · taloon.

prompts.q: The l-cases (-lla/-lta/-lle) translate which three English prepositions?
prompts.note: Exterior (surface) cases: pöydällä · pöydältä · pöydälle.

prompts.q: talossa vs pöydällä — which one means 'on'?
prompts.note: l-cases = surface (on the table); s-cases = interior (talossa — in the house).

prompts.q: Which case ending means “in / inside”?
prompts.note: Inessive. talossa — in the house; Helsingissä — in Helsinki.

prompts.q: Apply it: “in the shop” (kauppa) → ?
prompts.note: Two rules fire at once: KPT weakens pp→p, harmony picks -ssa (back vowels).

prompts.q: Apply it: “in Finland” (Suomi) → ?
prompts.note: i-final nouns often shift i→e in the stem: Suomi → Suome- + -ssa.

Finnish for 'to see'?
What does *äiti* mean?
Finnish for 'mother'?
Genitive (-n) of äiti?
prompts.note: KPT: t → d before a closing suffix, same pattern as katu → kadun.
